newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Analysts see 100 pct Brazil basic phone rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see 100 pct Brazil basic phone rate hike.

text.p: Brazil's basic residential telephone subscription rate is expected to double later this year as part of a restucturing to eliminate subsidies.
"I've made a comparison of subscription charges in other Latin American countries, and I'm projecting a rise from 3.74 reais to about 7.50 reais," said William Laurent of Flemings Securities.
Others projected a similar rise in basic rates, adding that reports Brasilia planned a 200 percent hike in the basic service rate to 11.22 reais seemed exaggerated.
The reports, which cited company President Francisco Xavier as saying that basic residential rates would be raised in November to 11.22 reais.
"A rate hike is planned for November but no one can say at this point what it will be," a Telebras spokesman said.
Nonetheless, some analysts said the reports were a sign the rate hike is likely to be higher than market expectations.
"I was considering an increase of only 100 percent but now I think it will be much higher," said Eduardo Munemori of Banco Pactual.
"My impression is that (Xavier) said something he shouldn't have and now they're trying to back-track, but I think it will be around" 200 percent, he added.

Analysts have known for months that a second round of rate adjustments are planned for late 1996 after last November's first phase of tariff restructuring raised basic service rates by 513 percent. Last year's rate hike has resulted in huge profits for Telebras and its 28 subsidiaries in 1996's first half.

But tariff adjustments also are seen as vital to preparing Brazil's telecoms sector for private competition and needed to eliminate Telebras long-distance unit Embratel's subsidy of local telephone service.
But analysts said Brazil is likely to raise basic rates to bring them in line with other regional telecoms firms.
"Eleven reais would be more than any other Latin American country," said Sergio Goldman, a telecoms analyst with BBA Paribas.
He said he was projecting a rise to about seven reais, compared with an equivalent of about eight in Argentina and seven in Mexico.
Goldman added the government also is likely to raise the tariff on extra pulses to between eight to 10 centavos from 5.3 centavos today, as well as lower long-distance and cellular phone rates.
Press reports of a possible 200-percent hike in Brazil's basic residential subscription rates sent Telebras shares soaring in morning trade in New York and Sao Paulo.
Prices dropped again after the company's spokesman said Xavier had been misunderstood and that he had not given a figure or percentage for the adjustment.

But analysts said the denial does not take the shine off Telebras shares. "We are very positive about the stock," Laurent said. "Whatever the adjustment, the news today can serve as a trigger to remind people that there will be a rate hike."
